posts.author: MrRyanBirth
posts.body:
Hey y'all, as I said, I'm really new to RPG Maker, like, bought it 5 days ago.
I thing it's time to make my ideas come true haha, I've been testing stuff, watching tutorials, etc...
I want to ask you for any tips, I know not to start by my "dream project" and to start small.
Any help is appreciated, thank you in advance!

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Welcome! There are kind of a bunch of "beginner tips" threads you might look through.
I strongly suggest:
- start with MZ's tutorial in the Help menu.
- supplement tutorials with the actual manual. Hit Help -> Contents and read about the different pages in the database.
- as you already know, start with small projects to learn how events and the default systems work.
- try Googling questions; between MZ and MV, they've been around for almost a decade.
When you have something to show off or ask for critiques, there's a maps and screenshots thread you can post in.
Game & Map Screenshots 12
Game & Map Screenshots 12   This thread is meant for showing off screenshots or maps made for your project, and to comment on or give advice to other members. Screenshots of any Maker (including Visual Novel Maker) is welcome. No other game engines are allowed.   In-game screenshots and maps...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Welcome to the forum and your journey with RPG Maker!
In addition to what was already said and what you already acknowledged, I would recommend actually recreating a bunch of tutorials and not just watch them. When you actually follow along and recreate the tutorial in a test project, your learning is reinforced by practical doing.
And, if you feel like it, you can always branch out from the tutorial and experiment with other things that catch your interest.
I recommend finding a YouTube content creator that has an entire series from the basics to more advanced and go through them all. By that time, you should be well equipped to just experiment with other stuff that you are thinking of.
Here is an excerpt of what I recommend for another person in another thread.
I searched for RPG MAKER MZ TUTORIALS and then looked for the top rated tutorials. Those are usually the ones who have been around the longest. Then I checked to see which videos were part of playlists. Then I looked at the playlists to see how many tutorials there were and what they covered.
I ended up just picking one to go all the way through. Then I sort of just spot picked tutorials from other series. And Caz has a series of 100 second videos that explain certain things pretty quickly.
And when I was recreating the tutorials, I also branched out and experimented on ideas as the inspiration hit me. That is also very useful.
Here are a few examples of creators with entire playlists that you might check out.
https://www.youtube.com/@LvLUpDesign/playlists
https://www.youtube.com/@rpggamemaker6684/playlists
https://www.youtube.com/@TheOdie/playlists
https://www.youtube.com/@DriftyG/playlists
https://www.youtube.com/@Cazwolf/playlists
Anyway, I hope some of these are helpful! I think I did the RPG Gamer Maker series along with samplings of other series. And some of these are new to me, but look interesting.
I don't specifically recommend my own tutorials because I sort of assume that anyone watching mine have already done more basic tutorials. Mine are just things I have experimented and built that I think might be helpful for someone. I don't start with the basics.
Good luck on your projects and remember to enjoy what you do!

posts.author: hernieren
posts.body: Welcome! I would advice focusing on mechanics first when starting a new game. Make the basic systems first and see if it's fun to play before moving forward. You don't know how many of us started our first game with the story, the characters, the mapping... before asking ourselves "how is this going to play?"

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Come on everybody, let's say our mantra!
3, 2, 1:
Start by making a small project!
Good job everyone, big pats on the back, now back to work. Jerrybot, stop getting high.
Start small, bookmark those ideas for later. For now, focus on learning through doing. Don't won't about plugins or advanced techniques, just make a cookie-cutter RPG Maker game to learn some basic function.
In no time you'll be standing here with us shouting the mantras from the roof tops.

posts.author: freakytapir
posts.body:
Start not even small, but don't start making the game until it all works. A single test room, with default art assets, and make sure everything runs.
Plugins by different makers? Add one by one, and test for conflicts.
Make sure you know what you want before you make a lot of stuff you don't need, I would say, but for your first project, ... throw stuff at the wall and see what sticks. Experiment. At this point, you getting to know the engine is the most important part.
Oh, and Just... Yanfly has some core plugins I almost consider mandatory at this point that allow you to break a lot of the enginnes default limits. I think there's a free starte pack of those.
Look at the stuff already on the database and try to see how it's made. That'll teach you to make your own stuff.
Polish is one of the last steps. Yes,  bit goes a long way. But a shiny but useless thing is still useless.

posts.author: ISC
posts.body: Besides the great advice you've already received, I would suggest you experiment. Experiment a lot without actually creating a game. Take an idea and experiment with the commands, the graphics, the plugins, and the mechanics you want to implement. This will take time and dedication, but it won't be wasted effort. When you start your own project (whether small or large), you'll find that the work done during the experimental phase will make it easier to create your game

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
I disagree with several posts above.
start with neither a big nor a small project, but with a scrap project.
Watching or reading a tutorial is never enough, you need to work through a tutorial doing its steps yourself to truly understand how to do something.
And for that there is no need to complete a game, just experiment in a project that you know to be scrapped before starting your true first game.
Other than that I suggest the starting point tutorial linked in my signature. It is somewhat old (I wrote it when VXA was current), but it goes about the very basics that are still unchanged through VXA, MV and MZ and are unlikely to change in the future either.
